# Synthetic example for the supplier acceptance test

**Everything here is synthetic** (generated by `research/tools/make-acceptance-sample.mjs` from fixed seeds). It is not data from the SWL DS07 or any other real device. It exists so the acceptance test can be tried, and so a reviewer can see what a report looks like.

| File | What it stands for |
|---|---|
| `P-SAMPLE-A.csv`, `P-SAMPLE-B.csv`, `P-SAMPLE-C.csv` | 12 nights per person, already mapped to the documented observation format. A travels to UTC+9 on night 7; B's firmware updates before night 6; C took the device off for an hour on night 5 (flagged `off_body`). |
| `P-SAMPLE-C-resync.csv` | The last ~3 nights sent again, as after an interrupted sync |
| `clock.csv` | Device clock vs a reference clock |
| `wear.csv` | When the device was known to be off the wrist |
| `bench.csv` | A reference thermometer during 12 samples |
| `profile.json` | The supplier profile: documented flags, planned firmware and time-zone changes, and written answers. Only one answer is filled in, and it is a placeholder. |
| `example-report.md` | The report these files produce |

**Run it:**

```bash
F=research/fixtures/acceptance-synthetic; node research/tools/supplier-acceptance.mjs --profile $F/profile.json --observations P-SAMPLE-A=$F/P-SAMPLE-A.csv --observations P-SAMPLE-B=$F/P-SAMPLE-B.csv --observations P-SAMPLE-C=$F/P-SAMPLE-C.csv --resync P-SAMPLE-C=$F/P-SAMPLE-C-resync.csv --clock $F/clock.csv --wear $F/wear.csv --bench $F/bench.csv --out /tmp/report.md
```

**Expected result:** all 12 file checks pass, and the verdict is still **not verified**. That is because the supplier's written answers (licence, data ownership and cloud, platform route, and so on) are missing and have not been reviewed. This is intended: a device is never accepted on its files alone.
